subject: Mutual Action Plan: Accelerated reserve + GPU pool scenarios for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Li <caroline@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: Accelerated reserve + GPU pool scenarios for Aurora Health

Hi Caroline / Aurora procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciate the candid feedback on inference latency targets for batch claims processing and the regulatory requirement around on-prem private pools for PHI workloads. As discussed, I pulled together a concise MAP with two close paths so we can lock capacity without blocking your validation timeline:

- Path A (Conservative): 4-month lead, dedicated H100 tranche (8x H100 nodes), staging window for SOC2 artifacts.
- Path B (Accelerated): 8-week lead with mixed Dedicated + Private burst (4x H100 dedicated + 4x private H100 on customer VPC), temporary quota uplift for initial eval.

Attached: MAP_Aurora_v1.xlsx (milestones + owners), h100_pool_model_v2.csv (cost/throughput sims), SLA_draft_Aurora_20261001.pdf (draft terms).

Requests / asks from Aurora to move Path B to a firm commitment:
1) Procurement confirms preferred payment cadence (monthly vs. quarterly prepay).
2) Security team shares SOC2 scoping hitlist by Oct 8 so we can start evidence collection.
3) Engineering provides a short list of the top-5 workloads (sample prompts/seq lengths) by Oct 6 for sizing validation.

Proposed mutual timeline (high level):
- Oct 6: engineering workload samples in hand
- Oct 8: security scoping confirmed
- Oct 15: sign-off on MAP and PO to reserve tranche
- Oct 30: Dedicated nodes provisioned & first staging slot

Ben / Marissa / Karthik: please review the milestone owners in the MAP and flag any gating items I missed.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: MAP_Aurora_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), h100_pool_model_v2.csv (csv), SLA_draft_Aurora_20261001.pdf (pdf)

From: Caroline Li <caroline@aurorahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurora Health Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Accelerated reserve + GPU pool scenarios for Aurora Health

Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear split between Path A and B. Path B aligns best with our executive ask to accelerate pilot into production by year-end, but a couple quick clarifications before we loop procurement: 

1) For Path B, can you confirm whether private VPC burst nodes require separate onboarding calendar with our networking team?
2) The SLA draft looks reasonable; we need a liability clause tweak around data residency (we prefer all PHI training traffic to stay inside our VPC).

I'll get the engineering samples to you by Oct 6. Procurement is trying to confirm budget cadence — I'll have an answer by Oct 5. Security will surface the SOC2 scoping doc early next week.

If you can provide a short note on the rollback/fallback policy in case dedicated nodes arrive late, that will help our CTO sign-off.

Thanks,
Caroline Li
Head of Product Ops | Aurora Health
caroline@aurorahealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Accelerated reserve + GPU pool scenarios for Aurora Health

Rishi — quick notes inline for the rollback / fallback language Caroline asked about. Suggest we offer a two-tier fallback plan:

- Fallback A (automatic): If Dedicated tranche starts >10 business days late, traffic temporarily routes to a compatible lower-cost instance family in our Hosted pool (same model quantized to int8) for up to 30 days while we prioritize Dedicated procurement. This preserves availability and reduces SLA credit exposure.
- Fallback B (manual): If Private VPC nodes cannot be onboarded due to networking windows, we spin up encrypted private-hosted nodes in Redwood-managed VPCs with customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) and an isolated tenancy window for the evaluation period. Requires procurement sign-off for interim hosting fees.

On sizing: the h100_pool_model_v2.csv has a scenario labeled "Mixed-burst-A" that maps to the 4+4 Path B. Karthik — recommend we add a short bucket-level SLO table to the MAP (p95 token latency targets per workload) so the customer can sign off on performance expectations up-front.

I can draft fallback text for the SLA and include the SLO table; want to keep the MAP light and push legal-level edits to the SLA draft.

- Ben
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Accelerated reserve + GPU pool scenarios for Aurora Health

Caroline — really appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary / next steps based on the thread and internal alignment: 

- We will proceed with Path B (Accelerated) tentative: reserve 4 Dedicated H100 nodes + capacity blueprint for 4 private VPC H100 nodes.
- Action items for Aurora: procurement confirms payment cadence by Oct 5 (Caroline), security shares SOC2 scoping list by Oct 8.
- Action items for Redwood: Ben to draft fallback language and a short SLO table by Oct 6; Marissa to open a provisioning ticket for the Dedicated tranche (internal ETA: provisioning slot request submitted Oct 7). Karthik will scope the networking onboarding checklist for private VPC by Oct 6.

If all asks complete on the proposed cadence we will translate the MAP into a PO + reservation statement and target provisioning window starting Oct 25 with staging in week-of Oct 30. I flagged the Path B cost delta in the h100_pool_model_v2.csv — happy to run a 1:1 with your procurement team to walk numbers.

Caroline, please reply-all to confirm procurement cadence and we will convert MAP_Aurora_v1.xlsx to a signed MAP and PO template.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
